To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) E2F3 is overexpressed in a high proportion of human prostate cancers; (ii) E2F overexpression is an independent factor predicting outcome in prostate cancer; (iii) E2F expression is associated with EZH2 expression in prostate cancer; and (iv) pRB expression in prostate cancers is associated with E2F3 and EZH2 expression.
E2F3 is a transcriptional activator of the EZH gene and that high levels of nuclear expression of both E2F3 and EZH2 are independent markers of poor prognosis in human prostate cancer.
